options: Rules and checks that make the answer come from the passages and make that checkable: citations, refusal, verification in code

stem: A citation the model wrote is…
options: A claim — it becomes evidence only when code verifies the id exists and the numbers appear in the cited passage
explanation: Verify in code; traceable is not proven, but it blocks invention.

stem: The model cites an id that was not among the provided passages. Code should…
options: Flag the answer for review — it cannot be checked and likely came from memory or invention
explanation: This is exactly what the id check exists for.

options: Every number in a sentence appears in the text of a passage that sentence cites
Asking the model if it is sure
explanation: It catches the commonest invention: a plausible figure.

stem: In the recorded run the uncovered question produced…
options: NOT_COVERED — retrieval returned the least-bad articles and the scoped model said no; route to a human
A citation to a random article
explanation: The system can say no, and code can tell that it did.

options: Lets users check, raises trust, and tells you which articles answer which questions — and which questions have none
explanation: A free signal about coverage gaps.

stem: The three routes after verification are…
options: Serve (clean), review (any unknown id / uncited claim / number not in source), escalate (NOT_COVERED)
explanation: Route on what the checks found.

stem: An answer passes every code check. It is…
options: Traceable, not proven — correctness still needs the golden-set eval and, where it matters, a human
explanation: Checks block invention; evals measure correctness.

stem: The model refuses questions the corpus covers. First things to check…
options: Retrieval (hit@k for those questions), a threshold set too high, a prompt rule too strict — measure refusal precision
explanation: Over-refusal erodes trust as fast as invention does.

stem: For claims code cannot check (paraphrased policy statements)…
options: Add a faithfulness judge and spot-check it
explanation: Code where you can, judges where you must, humans on a sample.
